title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
abstract: arXiv:2611.24249v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm fails on twin events: distinct physical executions recorded under identical task conditions. Collapsing the temporal dimension averages out transient cross-modal dynamics, effectively reducing physical event alignment to static scene recognition. Formally, we prove that as sequence length increases, any temporally pooled representation converges to the stationary recording condition. translated_title: 从点到轨迹：重新思考物理事件的多模态对齐
translated_abstract: 推进物理人工智能的发展需要超越静态物体识别，去理解现实世界的力学过程（如冲击、摩擦和力传递）如何随时间展开。虽然多模态对齐器试图通过匹配多传感器数据流来捕捉这些交互，但主流架构将每个时间序列压缩为单个池化嵌入。我们证明，这种范式在“孪生事件”上会失效：孪生事件是指在相同任务条件下记录的不同物理执行过程。将时间维度坍缩会平均掉瞬态的跨模态动态，实际上将物理事件对齐退化为静态场景识别。从形式上，我们证明随着序列长度的增加，任何时间池化表示都会收敛到稳定的录制条件。因此，随着时间窗口的增大，任何损失函数或嵌入几何都无法仅凭池化特征来区分孪生事件。相反，我们……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文证明主流多模态对齐方法将时间序列压缩为单一池化嵌入后无法区分相同任务条件下的不同物理执行（孪生事件），主张从静态“点”表示转向保留跨模态时间动态的“轨迹”级对齐来理解物理事件。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that temporally pooled multimodal embeddings fundamentally fail to distinguish twin physical events as sequence length grows, and advocates shifting from static point-based representations to trajectory-level alignment that preserves cross-modal temporal dynamics for physical event understanding.
